ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an NPN common-emitter amplifier. The emitter is connected to ground, the collector is connected through resistor R_C to the +12 V supply, and U_CE is marked from collector to emitter. There is also a base bias resistor R_B connected to the +12 V rail and coupling capacitors C1 and C2 at the input and output. Reasoning: On the DC load line, when the transistor is cut off, the collector current is approximately zero, so the voltage drop across R_C is nearly zero and U_CE is approximately the supply voltage, 12 V. The given static voltage is U_CE = 11 V, which is very close to 12 V. Therefore the quiescent operating point is near the voltage-axis intercept of the DC load line, corresponding to the cut-off region.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit: the image shows a common-emitter transistor with the emitter grounded and the collector fed from +12 V through RC. From the text, UCE = 11 V. Because the emitter is at ground, the collector is at about 11 V, so the voltage across RC is only 12 V - 11 V = 1 V. That means the collector current is small compared with the maximum load-line current, while saturation would require UCE to be low. A small collector current means the Q point is near cut-off. Thus the operating point is close to the cut-off region.
